scenes.narration: Do you know why your first prompt to Claude usually falls flat?
scenes.onscreen: why your first prompt falls flat?
scenes.visual: Coral 'Do you know...' pill, big headline, two question badges

scenes.narration: Most people type a few words, like, write an email. Then Claude has to guess the rest.
scenes.onscreen: A few words. Claude has to guess.
scenes.visual: Prompt card typing 'write an email', tilted 'Too vague' pill

scenes.narration: Instead, brief Claude like a brilliant new teammate, who knows nothing about your situation.
scenes.onscreen: Brief it like a new teammate.
scenes.visual: Headline, fact card with chat icon, source note

scenes.narration: Tell it three things. One, who it is for. Two, what you want. Three, what good looks like.
scenes.visual: Three numbered step cards appearing one by one

scenes.narration: For example. Write a short, friendly email to my landlord, asking to fix the heater this week.
scenes.onscreen: Write a short, friendly email to my landlord, asking to fix the heater this week.
scenes.visual: 'Try this' pill, prompt card typing the full prompt, three green tags

scenes.narration: Same Claude. A far better answer. Clear beats clever.
scenes.visual: Big word 'Clear', headline 'beats clever.', check fact card

scenes.narration: Follow Claude for all for more.

sources.claim: Anthropic's prompting guide says to be clear and direct, and to think of Claude as a brilliant but new employee who lacks context on your situation; more precise instructions give better responses
The three-part brief (who it is for, what you want, what good looks like) is this channel's own summary of that guidance, not a quote
